findings.headline: You say you charge for work done. Scheduling alone is billable.
findings.explanation: Book 40 appointments, write 20 notes, pay for 40. Telehealth calls count too, with or without a note.

claim_a.statement: Charge for jobs done, not access
claim_a.quote: Legacy EHRs charge for access. We charge for jobs done.

claim_b.quote: A session is counted each time you generate an AI note or schedule a session with a client

findings.why_not_just_wording: Scheduling is access, and access is the thing the headline says you do not charge for.
findings.caveat: The $69 cap bounds it, and the same answer says the fee covers the whole platform rather than the note.

findings.headline: Free claims offer runs on four pages. One of them says solo only.
findings.explanation: Group practices file the most claims and are the ones putting the wrong number in a budget.

claim_a.quote: $0.30 per claim submission, $0.15 per eligibility check

findings.why_not_just_wording: Three places state the offer with no limit and one limits it to a subset of customers.
findings.caveat: Four words on the pricing page fixes it. The restriction line also has a typo, so it looks like a late addition.

findings.headline: Trial is 30 days on one page and 14 days on another.
findings.explanation: The Group plan card sits under the 30-day claim and invites a team to start that trial.
findings.why_not_just_wording: Both pages present their number as the trial a team would get.
findings.caveat: The 14-day figure sits under a Legacy plans heading, and nothing marks where legacy ends on that page.

findings.headline: Canadian page prices card fees in C$ and claim fees in US$.
findings.explanation: A Canadian reader cannot tell whether a claim costs C$0.30 or roughly C$0.41.

claim_a.quote: Low fees for card transactions: 2.9% + C$0.30

claim_b.quote: $0.30 per claim submission, $0.15 per eligibility check

findings.why_not_just_wording: Every other price on the page is converted, so a bare dollar sign reads as a different currency.
findings.caveat: This looks like a localisation pass that skipped the insurance billing block.

findings.headline: Premium names your current tier and a discontinued $99 plan.
findings.explanation: Search for the price of Premium and you find $99, $69, or $1 per session capped at $69.

claim_a.quote: you won't be able to use features only included in our Premium plan

findings.why_not_just_wording: One name carries two prices and two billing models.
findings.caveat: Your FAQ says outright that pricing changed and links to the legacy page, which is more than most companies do.

findings.headline: One offer names a month now past. Another names no year.
findings.explanation: A reader cannot tell from either page whether the offer is open.
findings.why_not_just_wording: Both say when an offer applies and neither resolves to a date a reader can act on.
findings.caveat: The beta may have opened on time and the wording simply not been updated.

findings.headline: Treatment Plans are sold at no added cost and gated by plan.
findings.explanation: The feature page names no plan. The pricing page lists Treatment Plans as a comparison row, so it varies by tier.

claim_a.statement: No added cost, no plan named
claim_a.quote: Built into Upheal at no added cost.

claim_b.statement: A row in the plan comparison
claim_b.quote: Get insurance-compliant, AI-generated Treatment Plans, plus our Golden Thread feature to track client progress session-to-session.

findings.why_not_just_wording: No added cost answers the price question and leaves the entitlement question open.
findings.caveat: No added cost is fair if it means no add-on fee on top of your plan, which competitors do charge. The comparison table is built from divs, so we could not read which column holds it.

coverage_notes.what_was_not_checkable: Your support centre is the main gap. The collection pages we reached list article titles and nothing else, so none of the 186 help articles behind them was read. Account management, Client payments and Insurance billing are the three collections most likely to settle the findings above. upheal.io/terms returns a 404 from our crawl, so renewal, refund and price-change terms were not reviewed at all. The Group and Custom Enterprise plans publish no prices, so team pricing could not be checked for consistency. The plan comparison tables on all three pricing pages are built from styled divs rather than real tables, so per-plan values lose their column alignment when flattened to text. Nothing reported above depends on reading them.
